sanskrit_verse:
निक्षिप्तं वा परद्रव्यं नष्टं लब्ध्वापहृत्य वा ।
विक्रीयते ऽसमक्षं यद् विज्ञेयो ऽस्वामिविक्रयः ॥
transliteration: nikṣiptaṃ vā paradravyaṃ naṣṭaṃ labdhvāpahṛtya vā | vikrīyate 'samakṣaṃ yad vijñeyo 'svāmivikrayaḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When another's property, whether deposited, lost, or recovered, is sold without the owner’s presence or consent, it constitutes unauthorized alienation of ownership.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority: Ownership inheres in the original proprietor; no derivative claim supersedes it.
Causation: Transfer without consent disrupts lawful proprietary continuity.
Capacity-based responsibility: The actor bears full capacity-accountability for unauthorized disposal.
Restoration logic: The act demands reintegration of ownership integrity.
Consciousness alignment: Misalignment arises from violation of svāmin-dharma; correction realigns consciousness.
executable_legal_axioms: IF property ownership is NOT transferred by authorized proprietor THEN any transaction is null.
IF asset is sold without proprietor’s presence OR acknowledgment THEN action = unauthorized alienation.
IF unauthorized alienation occurs THEN automatic liability accrues to disposing agent.
IF unauthorized sale detected THEN ownership integrity MUST be restored via return or compensation protocol.
supreme_court_application: In adjudication at the highest level, where ownership claims are disputed post-unauthorized transfer, the threshold of responsibility lies solely with the unauthorized seller. No mitigating context overrides the fundamental breach of svāmitva-dharma. The court shall declare the transaction void and direct immediate restoration of title to the rightful owner.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that absence of proprietor consent invalidates transfer. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals how misaligned intent leads to disrupted dharma. Responsibility is proportional to the breach of svāmin-dharma. No punitive consequence is enacted—only the realignment of ownership integrity through conscious completion of duty.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate ownership verification process with proprietor’s acknowledgment.
Recover proceeds or item from unauthorized holder and return to lawful owner.
Require responsible party to undergo svāmin-dharma reorientation program.
Issue public record correction to reaffirm ownership authenticity.
final_declaration: By the authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, Source of all Dharma, this ruling restores svāmitva-integrity, aligns causal responsibility, and affirms that consciousness—not punishment—is the ultimate arbiter of justice.
